BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 1
5. TRANSMISSION SERVICE
RATE SCHEDULE 2801 – TRANSMISSION SERVICE – TIME-OF-USE
Availability For Customers who take service under Rate Schedule 1830 or are
eligible to take Service under Rate Schedule 1830 (Transmission
Service).
This Rate Schedule is not available to Customers taking service under Rate Schedule 1828 (Transmission Service – Biomass Energy
Program), Rate Schedule 1894 (Transmission Service – Clean BC
Industrial Electrification Rate – Clean Industry and Innovation) or Rate Schedule 1895 (Transmission Service – Clean BC Industrial
Electrification Rate – Fuel Switching). Customers will start Service under this Rate Schedule 2801 at the start
of their Billing Year. This Rate Schedule 2801 is a pilot effective until March 31, 2030.
Supply is at 60 kV or higher.
Termination This Rate Schedule will terminate effective March 31, 2030.
Date
Applicable in Integrated Service Area excluding the Districts of Kingsgate-Yahk and
Lardeau-Shutty Bench. ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026

BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 3
Definitions 1. Billing Year
The Billing Year is the 12-month period starting with the first day
of the Billing Period which commences nearest to April 1 in a
year, and ending on the last day of such 12-month period.
2. Billing Demand
The Billing Demand will be:
The highest kVA Demand during HLH in the Billing Period;
or 75% of the highest Billing Demand for the Customer's Plant
in the immediately preceding period of November to
February, both months included; or 50% of the Contract Demand stated in the Electricity Supply
Agreement for the Customer's Plant,
whichever is the highest value, provided that for new Customers
the Billing Demand for the initial two Billing Periods will be the
average of the daily highest kVA Demands for the Customer's
Plant. 3. High Load Hours (HLH)
HLH is the period of hours from 06:00 to 22:00 Monday to
Saturday, except for Statutory Holidays (New Year’s Day, Family
Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Canada Day, B.C. Day, Labour
Day, National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, Thanksgiving
Day, Remembrance Day and Christmas Day). 4. Low Load Hours (LLH)
Low Load Hours (LLH) are all hours other than HLH. ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026
ORDER NO. G-184-26 Electronically signed by Keshni Nan d
REGISTRAR

BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 4
5. Winter Period
The Winter Period comprises four Billing Periods starting with the
first day of the Billing Period that commences nearest to November 1 each year and ending on the last day of the fourth
Billing Period thereafter. 6. Winter On-Peak Period
The Winter On-Peak Period comprises the hours from 16:00 to
20:00 during the Winter Period weekdays excluding Statutory
Holidays (New Year’s Day, Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria
Day, Canada Day, B.C. Day, Labour Day, National Day for Truth
and Reconciliation, Thanksgiving Day, Remembrance Day and
Christmas Day). 7. Winter Off-Peak Period
The Winter Off-Peak Period comprises all other hours in the
Winter Period excluding the Winter On-Peak Period hours. 8. Spring Period
The Spring Period comprises the three Billing Periods starting
with the first day of the Billing Period that commences nearest to May 1 each year and ending on the last day of the third Billing
Period thereafter. 9. Remaining Period
The Remaining Period comprises all Billing Periods other than
the Winter Period and the Spring Period. 10. Pilot Period
The Pilot Period is April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2030.
ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026
ORDER NO. G-184-26 Electronically signed by Keshni Nan d
REGISTRAR

BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 5
Special 1. Customers must inform BC Hydro of their intention to enroll in
Conditions Rate Schedule 2801 by submitting a completed enrollment form
by March 19 for year 1 of the pilot, and March 1 in subsequent
years of the pilot to take service at the start of the next Billing
Year. 2. Customers that enroll in Rate Schedule 2801 for the 2026 Billing
Year will be enrolled for an initial term of three Billing Years.
Customers that enroll for subsequent Billing Years during the
Pilot Period will have an initial term that ends at the end of the
Pilot Period. For example, Customers that enroll in Rate Schedule 2801 for the 2027 Billing Year will be enrolled for
an initial term of three Billing Years, whereas Customers that enroll in Rate Schedule 2801 for the 2028 Billing Year will be
enrolled for an initial term of two Billing Years. 3. Customers may opt-out of Rate Schedule 2801 at the end of the
first Billing Year of their initial term by providing notice to
BC Hydro anytime before the end of their first Billing Year, with
the exception of Customers that have an Electricity Purchase
Agreement with BC Hydro. Those Customers must provide notice
to BC Hydro by the end of the third Billing Period of their second
Billing Year and their bills will be adjusted retroactively to the end
of the first Billing Year of their initial term. 4. Customers that opt-out of Rate Schedule 2801 at the end of their
first Billing Year may choose to enroll in Rate Schedule 2802,
Rate Schedule 2821 or Rate Schedule 2822 in a subsequent
Billing Year. 5. Customers that are enrolled in Rate Schedule 2801 may choose
to switch to Rate Schedule 2802, Rate Schedule 2821 or Rate
Schedule 2822 after their first Billing Year for the remainder of
their current term. For example, if a Customer has been enrolled in Rate Schedule 2801 for the first Billing Year of a three Billing
Year term, that Customer may switch to take service under ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026
ORDER NO. G-184-26 Electronically signed by Keshni Nan d
REGISTRAR

BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 6
Rate Schedule 2802 for the remaining two Billing Years of their
three Billing Year term. 6. Customers that enroll in Rate Schedule 2801 for the 2026 Billing
Year and have an initial term of three Billing Years will be
automatically re-enrolled for the remaining year of the Pilot Period (subject to Special Condition 3), unless they provide notice to
BC Hydro that they intend to opt-out of Rate Schedule 2801 at
the end of their initial term. Such notice must be provided to
BC Hydro by the end of their second Billing Year (i.e., the
Customer must provide one year notice). Customers that enroll in Rate Schedule 2801 after the 2026 Billing Year will automatically
remain enrolled in Rate Schedule 2801 until the end of the Pilot
Period, subject to Special Condition 3.
7. At the end of the first Billing Year during each Customer’s initial
three-year term, BC Hydro will provide a bill guarantee and
refund a Customer any positive total bill difference between what they were billed under Rate Schedule 2801 and what they would
have been billed under Rate Schedule 1830 based on actual
consumption during the Billing Year. This bill guarantee is only
available for the first year of each Customer’s initial term under Rate Schedule 2801 and it is offered on a one-time basis only.
For clarity, Customers will not receive any additional bill
guarantees regardless of whether they re-enroll in Rate Schedule 2802, Rate Schedule 2821 or
Rate Schedule 2822 under Special Condition 4 or switch their
rate under Special Condition 5.
8. Customers may not participate in the Industrial Load Curtailment
(ILC) Program while taking service under Rate Schedule 2801.
Notwithstanding Special Condition 6, if a Customer is taking
service under Rate Schedule 2801 and intends to participate in
the ILC Program, they may either: (i) remain on Rate Schedule 2801 until the start of the next Billing Year, at which time the
Customer may transfer from Rate Schedule 2801 to
Rate Schedule 1830 and begin participating in the ILC Program
ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026
ORDER NO. G-184-26 Electronically signed by Keshni Nan d
REGISTRAR

BC Hydro Rate Schedule 2801 – Revision 1
Effective: April 1, 2026
Section 5-2801 – Page 7
with no retroactive billing adjustment; or (ii) be accepted under the ILC Program and transfer from Rate Schedule 2801 to
Rate Schedule 1830 at the start of the next Billing Period to begin
participating in the ILC Program and have a retroactive billing
adjustment. The retroactive billing adjustment will be calculated
as the positive cumulative difference between the amount the Customer would have been billed under Rate Schedule 1830 and
the amount the Customer was billed under Rate Schedule 2801
based on actual consumption for the period from the start of the
current Billing Year to the end of the last Billing Period that the Customer took service under Rate Schedule 2801. Customers
that transfer from Rate Schedule 2801 to Rate Schedule 1830 to
participate in the ILC Program may transfer back from Rate Schedule 1830 to Rate Schedule 2801 in a subsequent
Billing Year. 9. Customers with self-generation facilities taking service under
Rate Schedule 2801 are precluded from taking service under
Rate Schedule 1880 during Winter On-Peak Periods.
Taxes The rates set out in this Rate Schedule are exclusive of goods and
services and provincial sales taxes. Rate Riders The Deferral Account Rate Rider as set out in Rate Schedule 1901
applies to all charges payable under this Rate Schedule, before taxes
and levies. The Trade Income Rate Rider as set out in Rate Schedule 1904
applies to all charges payable under this Rate Schedule, before taxes
and levies.
Note The terms and conditions under which Transmission Service is supplied are contained in Electric Tariff Supplement Nos. 5 and 6, or
Electric Tariff Supplement Nos. 87 and 88, as applicable.
Rate Increase Effective April 1, 2026, the rates under this Rate Schedule include a
rate increase of 0.59% before rounding.
ACCEPTED: September 21, 2026
ORDER NO. G-184-26 Electronically signed by Keshni Nan d
